name: Economics
notes: Declaration: C average or better in at least three of ECON 108/207/209/230/one semester of calculus; no pass/fail credit toward the major.
ECON 108 cannot be taken after ECON 207; honors equivalents accepted for 207/209.
Electives: no pass/fail; ECON 394 and ECON 230 cannot count; ECON 390 once; graduate (400-level) courses count with instructor permission; 8-credit courses count as one elective.
Department overlap policy matches the app's defaults (3 with a second major, 2 with a minor, 1 with a cluster); the calculus requirement and ECON 230 are overlap-exempt.
Transfer: freshmen-entry students may transfer at most one core course and two electives (allied-field counts as elective).
An honors BA variant exists (adds ECON 207H/208/219 and 389W or 289W, with GPA thresholds) - not separately modeled.

requirementGroups.label: Core
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: ECON 108: Principles of Economics; ECON 207: Intermediate Microeconomics; ECON 209: Intermediate Macroeconomics; ... ECON 231W: Econometrics

requirementGroups.label: Statistics (ECON 230 or substitute)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: The following can be used to substitute for ECON 230: STAT 190 ..., MATH 203: Introduction to Mathematical Statistics, or DSCC 262 Computational Introduction to Statistics

requirementGroups.label: Calculus sequence
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Students are required to complete one of the following calculus sequences: MATH 141, MATH 142 and MATH 143; MATH 161 and MATH 162; MATH 171 and MATH 172

requirementGroups.label: Economics electives (4)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Four economics electives ... ECON 394: Internship and ECON 230: Economic Statistics cannot be counted as electives
requirementGroups.note: Graduate 400-level courses can also count (not matched by this filter); see notes.

requirementGroups.label: Allied field (2 courses, same field)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Students are required to complete two 200-level (or above) courses in the same allied field. ... Acceptable Allied Fields: Computer science; Data science; Environmental Science or Environmental Studies; Health Policy; History; Mathematics ...; Political science; Psychology; Statistics; Undergraduate Business Program courses
requirementGroups.note: NEEDS nuance: the same-field constraint (and the business-program option) is not auto-enforced; cross-field pairs require a department petition.

upperLevelWriting.label: Two of the major's courses taken for W credit
upperLevelWriting.sourceQuote: Upper-level writing requirement (two of the above courses must be taken for W credit)
